prompt:
Create a single instructional gardening illustration on a genuinely transparent background, landscape 3:2. The supplied image is STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: match this book's clear coloured pencil and watercolour instructional illustration, warm tan earth, restrained texture, fine edges and realistic simplified proportions. Do not copy the supplied plant, hand or subjects.
Show a cutaway cross-section of a PREPARED PLANTING POCKET, before the young courgette is planted. A broad slice of ordinary light-brown garden soil, with a rounded rectangular area in its centre about equally deep and wide. This central area was dug out and has been completely refilled with garden soil MIXED with mature compost: render it as moderately darker crumbly brown soil, with a few organic flecks. Show a clear contrast with the surrounding tan soil but a natural permeable edge: NO pot, NO liner, NO bucket, NO bricks, NO closed wall. The central enriched area is NOT an empty hole and NOT a layer of pure manure. Its surface makes a very slight broad mound above the adjacent level soil, only about one tenth the depth of the pocket. The soil slice is about twice as wide as the central pocket and slightly deeper than it. Show the whole cross-section, with modest transparent margins. No plant, no seed, no roots, no tools, no hands, no grass or scenery. Keep the diagram simple and unmistakable at a small printed size. No text, labels, numbers, arrows, dimensions, border or background.

transplantRevision.prompt:
Edit the FIRST reference image for an instructional gardening book. Keep its recognisable young courgette seedling, hand supporting the root ball from the right, warm coloured-pencil and watercolour drawing style, restrained tan/brown earth palette and simple readable composition. Change the ground to a CLEAR CUTAWAY OF A PREPARED PLANTING POCKET, matching the SECOND reference. The second reference supplies the soil-pocket structure and colours only.
Show a broad cross-section of ordinary pale tan soil. In its centre is a large roughly square pocket, about equally deep and wide, fully refilled with moderately dark brown soil mixed with mature compost, with a gently rounded base, a permeable natural boundary and a very slight mound. The enriched pocket must be substantially wider and deeper than the small transplant root ball: the root ball should occupy about one third of the pocket's width and one third of its depth, and the rich mix must be plainly visible beside AND below it. At the top centre, the hand is lowering the small courgette root ball into a small planting opening within the enriched pocket. The top of the root ball is nearly level with the slight mound, with the green stem and leaves above soil level. The narrow root ball can be a slightly darker brown with a few visible pale roots so that it is distinct from the larger prepared pocket.
Make the whole causal sequence unmistakable: ordinary pale soil outside, a much larger darker compost-enriched pocket inside it, small seedling root ball being planted into the top of that pocket. No pot or liner remains in the ground; no boards, deep empty pit, open chasm, unrelated tools, duplicate plants or labels. Preserve botanically plausible leaf and stem attachments and a natural hand. Use a landscape 3:2 composition, including all the plant, hand and cutaway soil silhouette with a small clear margin. GENUINELY TRANSPARENT background, no opaque background, shadow or halo outside the isolated illustration. No text, border or decorative elements. This must read clearly as one small illustration in a three-picture book sequence.
transplantRevision.requestedChange: Show the transplant being planted into the prepared compost-enriched pocket rather than ordinary soil; bottom-align all three planting illustrations.
transplantRevision.visualCheck: Tan soil outside a larger dark enriched pocket, with smaller rooted plug at the top and enriched mix visible beside and below it. Original instructional style, seedling and hand retained.
